primaryFinding.title: The silent-fabricated-zero guard fails open on page wording, not on any county-specific code branch -- every county whose portal doesn't literally render the English string 'N Total Results' is silently exposed right now, and nothing counts or observes it
primaryFinding.origin: Corrected mid-close by doc-repo-31, who first proposed a narrower closing framing (defect class verified on the shared path via McLennan, Hays residual is access-only) after this lane's code trace found no county-specific branch, then WITHDREW that recommendation on rereading the guard's own implementation. Recorded here as the primary finding per their explicit instruction, not softened into a Hays-only statement.
primaryFinding.mechanism: playwrightBrowser.ts:91-101, createPlaywrightBrowser().extractTotalResultsHint(): reads document.body.innerText, matches it against the single regex /([\d,]+)\s+Total\s+Results/i, returns null on no match. searchPostProcess.ts:56, finalizeIndexSearchWithAcquisition(): when hits.length === 0, calls `input.browser.extractTotalResultsHint?.()` (optional chaining) and refuses (needs-human/index-hit-extraction-unsupported) ONLY if the hint is a positive number; any other outcome falls through to `status: complete` with zero hits -- the exact fabricated-zero shape this whole gate exists to catch.
threeFailOpenPaths: 1. Vendor wording differs from the one hard-coded English phrase ('Showing 1-20 of 1,706', '1706 records found', a count in an iframe or shadow DOM outside document.body.innerText): regex misses, hint is null, guard is skipped, complete/zero returned.

2. page.evaluate() throws for any reason (navigation mid-read, detached frame, anything): the try/catch at playwrightBrowser.ts:98-100 swallows it and returns null -- a guard that cannot run silently passes, and what passes is 'report zero records'.

3. searchPostProcess.ts:56 calls the method via optional chaining (`?.()`); any RecordsRecipeBrowser implementation that does not define extractTotalResultsHint returns undefined with no error at all, same silent skip.
primaryFinding.testCoverageIsWorseThanAbsent: searchPostProcess.test.ts:37-48 DOES cover the hint-undefined path, but the test asserts and locks in the fail-open behavior as INTENDED: `mockBrowser()` with extractTotalResultsHint not implemented, comment reads 'no regression for portals without the signal, e.g. Hays', assertion is `expect(result.status).toBe("complete")`. Hays is named in the test suite itself as the reference example of a portal expected to silently return complete/zero. This is not a coverage gap; it is the current design intent, asserted and green.
primaryFinding.exposureIsUnobserved: Grepped the full records-request-worker src tree, scripts/p85/*, and api-server's records_request_jobs consumers for any counter, metric, canary check, or audit of 'complete' results with zero indexHits and a null/absent portalDeclaredResultCount hint. Found none -- only the implementation and its two test files reference the hint at all. The exposure is not merely unfixed; no signal exists anywhere that would tell anyone it is happening in production today, for Hays or any other county.
primaryFinding.scopeOfCorrection: NOT FIXED by this lane, deliberately. doc-repo-31's explicit instruction: the two remediation shapes (a second independently-derived signal for portal-declared-result-presence, or making the guard fail CLOSED by default -- refuse whenever the hint is null/absent rather than only when it's a disagreeing positive number) both change refusal behavior for every county on every job, which is an operator scope decision, not this lane's or tonight's.

17b-gate.additionalFollowUp: Per doc-repo-31's request, traced whether the shared results-extraction/zero-hits decision code (searchPostProcess.ts, indexHits.ts, playwrightBrowser.ts) has any Hays-specific or county-specific branch that would prevent McLennan's passing live result from transferring as evidence for Hays. Found none at the CODE level: vendorFamilyFromPortalId() explicitly groups hays-erss and mclennan-online-records into the same 'tyler' vendor family; extractTotalResultsHint() is one generic, unparameterized implementation; the single finalizeIndexSearchWithAcquisition() call site is unconditional for both portals. doc-repo-31 initially proposed closing the gate on that basis (defect class verified on the shared path via McLennan; Hays residual is access-only), then WITHDREW that recommendation on rereading extractTotalResultsHint's own implementation: the guard is not a code branch, it is a presence check against one hard-coded English phrase in page text, and it fails open (see primaryFinding above) in ways that have nothing to do with which county's code path runs. McLennan's passing result only proves the guard fires when the vendor's page literally says 'N Total Results' -- which McLennan's does. Hays's page wording was never observed, because the probe never reached that step. The corrected, narrower true statement: the DECISION CODE is shared and passed on McLennan; whether HAYS'S PAGE WOULD TRIP THE SAME GUARD is still unknown and is one instance of a fleet-wide unobserved exposure, not a county-specific question.

whatRemainsOpen: PRIMARY: the silent-fabricated-zero guard (extractTotalResultsHint, playwrightBrowser.ts:91-101) fails open for any county whose portal doesn't literally render 'N Total Results', for any browser-read error, and for any recipe that omits the optional method -- three named, code-cited fail-open paths, test-locked as intended behavior (searchPostProcess.test.ts:37-48 names Hays as the expected-complete-on-zero-hint example), and completely unobserved in production (no counter/metric/audit anywhere counts complete-with-zero-hits-and-null-hint occurrences). This is a control-design gap general to every county on this recipe family, not a Hays-specific fact. NOT fixed by this lane -- both remediation shapes (an independent presence signal, or flipping the guard to fail closed by default) change refusal behavior fleet-wide and are the operator's scope call, per doc-repo-31's explicit instruction.

17b-gate's original, narrower question (is the defect present or absent specifically on Hays) is still not directly answered -- the probe never reached results-extraction, so Hays's own page wording relative to the guard's hard-coded phrase was never observed. Whether the broader finding above is sufficient to answer 17b-gate's intent, or whether Hays additionally needs its own resolution path past the reCAPTCHA wall (headed browser, human-solve, or a different verification route), is doc-repo-31/operator's call, not this lane's.
Items 17a and 17b (21 held-job re-runs) remain entirely with the operator, unstarted by design.
